title: Ge/ZnS 24-Layer with Tight ±15% Bound Constraints and Interior-Point Solver
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining layer thicknesses to ±15% of quarter-wave baseline values (550±82.5 nm for Ge, 900±135 nm for ZnS) while using an interior-point optimizer that penalizes large inter-layer thickness ratios will improve optimization convergence and maintain the coherent half-wave stacking foundation, yielding target scores comparable to or exceeding prior 24-layer results (0.960).
design_principle: Trust-region optimization around verified baseline preserves the physical cavity resonance structure while allowing localized impedance tuning. Tight bounds prevent the optimizer from exploring physically unrealistic thickness combinations that degrade spectral performance.
proposed_topology: Air | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | Ge(550nm) | ZnS(900nm) | CaF2 substrate. Total 24 finite layers with alternating Ge/ZnS sequence starting with Ge.
design_variables: layer thicknesses with bounds 467.5-632.5 nm for Ge layers, 765-1035 nm for ZnS layers
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: ±15% thickness tolerance represents realistic deposition control
Ge and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for Fabry-Perot cavity formation
Transfer-matrix method for coherent multilayer interference
Trust-region optimization for bounded parameter spaces
expected_advantages: Tighter bounds prevent optimizer from exploring non-physical regions
Interior-point solver handles bound constraints naturally
Preserves cavity resonance structure from baseline design
May achieve better convergence than unconstrained gradient descent
known_risks: Bounds may be too restrictive to find global optimum
24-layer stack showed lower scores than 20-layer in prior iterations
Ge absorption may limit peak transmittance in target bands
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating Ge/ZnS multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate under normal incidence from air ambient. Layer sequence: Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS-Ge-ZnS (24 finite layers total). Initialize all Ge layers at 550 nm with optimization bounds [467.5, 632.5] nm. Initialize all ZnS layers at 900 nm with optimization bounds [765, 1035] nm. Use coherent TMM solver across wavelength range 3600-5200 nm. Optimize for four objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4150-4350 nm band, maximize mean transmittance in 4550-4750 nm band, minimize mean transmittance in 3600-4000 nm band, minimize mean transmittance in 4850-5200 nm band. Use interior-point or trust-region optimizer that penalizes large inter-layer thickness ratios. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive: tight ±15% bound constraints around baseline QW values with interior-point solver to preserve coherent half-wave stacking while permitting localized impedance tuning.
